aboutInfo: This adapter is free and open source. If you find it useful, please consider supporting its development with a small donation.
authInfo: Note: Authentication is optional. The display will always go through the authentication flow, but credentials are only validated if this option is enabled.
authRequiredTooltip: If enabled, devices must enter valid credentials to authenticate
portTooltip: Port the HA clients connect to – default 8123, like Home Assistant; the check warns when another instance already holds it
bindTooltip: Select the network interface to listen on (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces)
mdnsEnabledTooltip: Broadcast the service via mDNS so devices can find it automatically (works on all platforms)
mdnsInfo:
mDNS broadcasts the service on the local network so devices can discover it automatically.

If mDNS is disabled or not working, enter the URL manually on the display:
`http://YOUR_IP:8123`
proxyInfo: Only enable when running BEHIND a trusted reverse proxy that terminates TLS (e.g. nginx, Traefik). The proxy must strip incoming X-Forwarded-* headers — otherwise clients can spoof their IP, which corrupts client identification and the per-IP protection limits. With this on, cookies are marked `Secure` when X-Forwarded-Proto is `https`.
redirectInfo: Redirect targets are set via datapoints, not here. Use `global.mode` + `global.enabled` to send every display to the same URL, or set each display under `clients.<id>.mode`. In the `mode` dropdown pick a discovered URL, or choose `manual` and enter any URL in the matching `manualUrl` datapoint.
serviceNameTooltip: Name shown on the display during discovery
trustProxyTooltip: Switch on only if a reverse proxy (e.g. nginx) sits in front of the adapter. The adapter then takes the display's address from the proxy. Without such a proxy, any device could fake its address.
globalEnabled: Apply the global URL to all displays
globalEnabledDesc: Master switch. On: every display follows the global URL. Off: every display shows its landing page until you pick a mode.
globalModeDesc: Only affects displays whose mode is set to Global URL. Use the master switch to apply the global URL to every display at once.
globalManualUrlDesc: The URL used when the global redirect mode is set to Manual URL.
clientModeDesc: Where this display redirects: a discovered dashboard, Global URL to follow the global setting, Manual URL to use the manualUrl datapoint, or --- to show the landing page.
clientManualUrlDesc: The URL this display opens when its redirect mode is set to Manual URL.
clientResolvedUrlDesc: The URL this display was last sent to. Empty means it shows the landing page.
clientRemoveDesc: Write true to delete this display's folder and all its states — on its next request it reappears as a new entry showing the landing page.
refreshUrlsDesc: Write true to re-scan the broker for VIS/VIS-2 projects, Admin tiles and other discovered URLs. Useful after creating a new VIS view without restarting the adapter.
pageConnectedSubhead: This display is linked to ioBroker. Choose a redirect URL to finish setup.
pageSetupIntro: Set the URL that this display should open on next refresh:
pageStep1: Open the ioBroker admin and switch to the Objects view.
pageStep3: In the mode dropdown, pick a discovered dashboard — or choose Manual URL and paste any URL (VIS, Grafana, …) into the manualUrl datapoint.
pageAutoRefresh: This page refreshes automatically every 15 seconds.
pageOfflineSubhead: hassemu is not answering. As soon as it is reachable again, this display returns to its dashboard by itself.
pageTargetOfflineSubhead: hassemu is running, but the configured target does not respond. As soon as it is reachable again, this display reloads automatically.
passwordRequiredWhenAuth: A password is required when authentication is enabled.
authSubtitle: Sign in to authorize this display.
authErrorHint: Please check the server address and try onboarding the display again.
authErrorResponseType: This server only accepts sign-in requests with response_type=code.
authErrorRequest: The sign-in request lacks client_id or redirect_uri, or one of them is not valid.
authErrorRedirectUri: The address the sign-in should return to (redirect_uri) is not allowed for this app.
authContinueHint: This sign-in hands an access code to the address below. Continue only if you started the sign-in yourself.
healthInfo: Uptime monitors and container health checks: use http://YOUR_IP:8123/health — it answers without creating a display entry. A request to / counts as a new display.
secureTooltip: Encrypts login, password and tokens with a certificate from ioBroker; off, everything stays plain HTTP
httpsInfo: With HTTPS the displays reach hassemu under the name in the certificate instead of the IP address, so that name must resolve on every display. With ioBroker's default certificate (self-signed, issued for the computer name) an Android display needs both: the certificate installed as trusted, and a network that resolves the computer name. A dashboard on plain HTTP cannot be shown inside an HTTPS page — choose an HTTPS address for it. Switching HTTPS on changes the address of hassemu: every display shows up once as a new device and must be pointed at the new address.
